newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Boral says float better than trade sale.
newsitem.headline: Boral says float better than trade sale.

text.p: Australian industrial group Boral Ltd said the planned public float of its gas distribution network would achieve a higher price than through a trade sale, and that the security offered will be a stapled security.

Boral announced on Monday that it expected to receive proceeds of more than A$850 million from the sale, which would see the creation of a company to be known as Envestra Ltd in which Boral would hold a 19.9 equity investment.
"We are acheiving a price for these higher than what would have been achieved through a trade sale," managing director Tony Berg told a news conference.
Berg said the float would be attractively priced for the public and institutions. A prospectus was expected to be released in July.
"The security that will be offered is a stapled security -- in other words it will be a share and a note." he said.
This was similar to some other infrastructure vehicles.

"The reason that it is potentially attractive to investors is that we're talking here about a utility which has a natural monopoly, so there isn't the normal business risk that applies to all other businesses," Berg said.
Proceeds from the sale would be initially used to retire debt, but would also enable Boral to purchase other assets.

"This puts us in a position to be a bidder for other assets when they do become available, and I guess the prime example of that in the gas area is the privatisation of the Victorian gas assets," Berg said.
Boral had worked on the float for a considerable time, and Berg said it was an exciting transaction as it met a number of Boral's objectives.
"We're very confident about the float," Berg said.
